params.rule_applied: Best ceiling in the registered primary analysis is 0.273, at or below the 0.30 branch boundary.
params.primary_analysis: Monthly evaluation dates, Newey-West standard errors at lag ceil(h/21)-1, as registered. No horizon beats the 20-day baseline. Ceilings fall at 60 and 120 days and only partially recover at 250.
params.monotonicity_check: Also fails. Nothing rises with horizon; every factor dips at 60 days. The registration committed in advance to reading a non-monotone pattern as noise.
params.unregistered_degree_of_freedom_found: The registered non-overlapping robustness check specifies every k-th month-end but not which of the k phases to start from. The first computed phase showed ceilings of 0.455 (momentum_6m, 120d) and 0.311 (momentum_3m, 60d), both of which would have supported the hypothesis. This was not registered and the favourable reading was not reported as a result.
params.phase_sensitivity_check: Run post hoc, disclosed as such. Across all phases the 120-day momentum_6m ceiling spans -0.250 to +0.509 with a median of 0.175, below the 0.236 baseline. The phase originally computed was among the most favourable available in several cells. Read across all phases the robustness check agrees with the primary analysis.
params.conclusion: Lengthening the forward horizon does not raise the achievable ceiling for cross-sectional momentum on this asset class. Combined with the P4 finding that universe size is not a lever, no structural lever has been identified, and the 0.30 threshold remains unreachable and unmeasurable on this data.
params.scope_limit: Two momentum factors on one eleven-name ETF layer over one in-sample window. It does not speak to other factor families, other asset classes, or a differently specified signal.
